title: Probabilistic Attention for Sequential Recommendation

problem.claim: Sequential recommendation must model users' dynamic preferences from historical interactions while balancing relevance and diversity.

gap.claim: Existing Transformer-based approaches lack a clear SR-specific definition of self-attention, overlook global item-pair context, and prioritize relevance over diversity.

contributions.claim: Attention is defined as dependency interactions among items, quantified under a global probabilistic model through probabilities of corresponding item subsets.
The work transforms repulsive interactions from Determinantal Point Processes into a DPP-kernel-based attention mechanism for sequential recommendation.
The resulting Probabilistic Attention mechanism, PAtt, directly considers category or topic distribution to enhance recommendation diversity.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors introduce a fresh perspective for explaining attention in sequential recommendation and a distinctive attention mechanism tailored to that setting.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that the attention mechanism has excellent scalability and adaptability.
The authors report significant improvements in recommendation performance for both relevance and diversity.

narrative_sequence.summary: Sequential recommendation models users' changing preferences from historical interactions, and Transformers have benefited the task through long-range pairwise relationships.
Existing approaches lack an SR-specific account of attention, omit global pair prevalence, and neglect diversity.
The paper defines attention probabilistically as item dependency interactions and uses DPP repulsive interactions to design a tailored kernel.
The resulting PAtt mechanism is reported to improve both relevance and diversity while offering scalability and adaptability.

source_observation.claim: Modeling global item dependencies and repulsive interactions can expose information missed by pairwise relevance computations.

interpretation.claim: A probabilistic formulation may align the attention mechanism more closely with recommendation objectives than directly reusing a generic Transformer component.

application.claim: When designing sequential recommenders, incorporate global context and explicit diversity-sensitive interactions into the attention mechanism.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether this approach improves outcomes outside the reported recommendation setting or under different evaluation conditions.

unknowns: Datasets, baselines, metrics, and quantitative result values are not specified.
Implementation details and computational resource requirements are not specified.
The abstract does not provide independent verification of the reported findings.
